Evil Dead Burn: Every Alleged Leak From Those L.A. Test Screenings (And What's Actually Real)

story // Jul 3, 2026

Watch on YouTube

⚠ MASSIVE SPOILER WARNING. We're about to gut this thing open. If you want Burn to hit you cold in the theater, close the tab and come back July 11. Still here? Good. Let's get nasty.

Alright, so the internet's been on fire (pun absolutely intended) after some early test screenings of Evil Dead Burn reportedly went down in Los Angeles, and the "leaks" have been flying. A lot of it lines up with stuff we've already confirmed through legit reporting. Some of it is straight-up fan fanfiction wearing a trench coat. As a house that's had "Dawn of the Dead" baked into its name since day one, we're gonna do you the courtesy of telling you which is which. Grab your boomstick.

The Tone: Mean, Nasty, and Zero Goofiness

First thing every screener agreed on — this ain't Army of Darkness. There's no slapstick. No "hail to the king, baby." Instead, folks are describing it as a "mean, nasty, New French Extremity–style nightmare," which, if you know that particular corner of horror, means Vaníček came to make you deeply uncomfortable and leave you there. This tracks hard with everything the director's said in the actual press. Verdict: confirmed vibe.

New to the sandbox? A possessed, Deadite dog. The franchise has danced around animal possession for decades (that cackling deer head in Evil Dead II doesn't count), so a full-on demon hound in a mainline theatrical entry is a genuine first. Verdict: confirmed.

The Plot: Jessica, the Crash, and a Family That Should've Known Better

Burn reportedly picks up Jessica's thread from that lakeside cabin stinger at the end of Evil Dead Rise. Word is she's the one who causes the car crash that takes out Will — husband to our lead, Alice — which is the whole reason Alice ends up seeking comfort at the in-laws' remote family home. Spoiler: comfort is not on the menu. Verdict: confirmed.

Here's where it gets juicy for the lore hounds. The film ties directly back to Fede Álvarez's 2013 Evil Dead. Will's grandfather was an occult investigator who tracked down the Kandarian Dagger, hoarded newspaper clippings about the 2013 cabin massacre, and — this is the good part — stitched together his own DIY Necronomicon. A homemade Book of the Dead. Which means this family didn't stumble into the evil by accident. Grandpa went looking for it. Verdict: confirmed.

The theory the leaks run with: the Kandarian demons are drawn to that homemade journal and are hunting this specific bloodline — either for straight-up revenge against grandpa's meddling, or to satisfy some bigger lore prophecy. That "vengeance" read is speculation, but it's good speculation and it fits the mythology like a glove. Verdict: plausible theory, not confirmed.

The Incantation Mishap & The Inferno Deadite

Allegedly, Alice finds grandpa's journal and reads an incantation — but doesn't finish it. Screeners compared this to Ash botching the graveyard chant in Army of Darkness: instead of handing the dead a formal invite to possess the living, she basically rings the dinner bell and tells them exactly where the book is. Whoops. Verdict: unverified plot detail — treat as leak.

And the final boss. Oh, the final boss. Will gets resurrected as the movie's big bad — the "Inferno Deadite," described as a constantly-burning husk brought to life mostly through real practical fire effects. Alice having to throw down against the literal flaming corpse of the husband she's still grieving? That's the kind of emotional gut-punch this franchise doesn't usually swing for. We are so in. Verdict: confirmed.

The Post-Credits Scene: Here's Where the Leak Gets Sketchy

Okay, real talk. The spiciest claim floating around is that the director deliberately pulled the post-credits scene from the test screenings to avoid spoilers, and that it teases the return of a major — probably female — legacy character. The popular guess? Mia, the survivor of the 2013 massacre, because of how hard Burn leans on that film.

XFD REALITY CHECK: We could not verify this one anywhere legit. A post-credits scene does exist — a reactor from the July 1 embargo-lifted screenings confirmed there's a stinger worth staying for — but nobody credible has described what's in it, and the "director cut it from screenings" + "it's Mia" stuff reads like fan theory dressed up as insider intel. Fun to chew on. Don't tattoo it on yourself.

Our two cents? Mia coming back would rip. But if we're betting, the franchise has a history of Ash-flavored stingers, and the door's wide open for a tie-in to the 1972 prequel Evil Dead Wrath coming in 2028. We'll know for sure once the review embargo fully drops and someone brave livetweets the credits.

The XFD Bottom Line

Strip away the sketchy post-credits rumor and what's left is a Evil Dead entry that sounds genuinely vicious — practical gore, real fire, a demon dog, a homemade Book of the Dead, and a final boss engineered to break your heart before it breaks your body. If the screeners are right, Vaníček understood the assignment and then set the assignment on fire.

Evil Dead Burn claws into theaters July 10. We'll be there opening night, and we'll circle back once the credits scene stops being a mystery. Stay nasty.

UPDATE — Burn is in theaters now and we've published our full Evil Dead Burn review. Short version: the leaks we marked confirmed above landed almost exactly as described, and that post-credits rumor is finally settled. Go see how the scorecard held up.
